![A project dashboard page in Genos with headline numbers, a milestone bar and who holds the open work](/lp/guide/en/dashboard.webp)

It is the day of the status meeting. Someone will ask where the launch stands, and you are the one expected to know.

## Why it is hard

The answer is spread across the task list. You count what is done, look for what is overdue, ask two people what is stuck, and put it into a slide or a message. By the time the next meeting comes round, it is out of date and you start again.

Meanwhile everyone who wants the picture between meetings interrupts you for it.

## How Genos helps

Schedule a **Dashboard page** once. Pick what it covers: one milestone, one project, or your own progress. Choose how far back the numbers go and when it runs. The first run saves a page in your notes; each later run replaces it with new numbers, at most once a day, or whenever you press **Run now**.

```flow
Schedule it once
Each run replaces the page
Open it from your Inbox
Click through to the task
```

The page is mostly pictures. A milestone page shows how much is done, what is overdue, blocked or without an owner, what is left by due date, and who holds the open work. Where there is enough to go on, it also says whether the milestone looks on track, tight or at risk, based on what was closed in the last 14 days and assuming no new tasks.

## What you get

- **No weekly rebuild.** The page you opened last week is the same page, with this week's numbers.
- **Problems you can act on.** The tasks it lists are links, so "two are blocked" is one click from which two.
- **A page you can share.** Save it where the right people can read it, or share it. At every run Genos checks who can read the page. It names only what every reader may open, and a project or milestone page does not run if a reader is not on that project.
- **Less "any update?"** People who can open the page can look for themselves.

A plain dashboard uses no AI. Where your Genos offers it, you can add a short AI summary, which uses AI credits.

## How to start

Dashboards are on Core and above.

1. Open **Settings → Genos → Genos Assist Schedules** and add a schedule.
2. Choose **Dashboard page**, then the milestone or project.
3. Pick the days and time, for example the morning of your status meeting.
4. Choose who can read it under **Save to**.

You will find your dashboards again under **Custom dashboards by AI** in Task Stats.
